solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some modern art is appealing, with time yielding to nonsense, crudely

indicators.note: one thing yielding to another gives up its place, so a letter is swapped out for the slang that follows

blocks.note: something appealing draws people in
T is the abbreviation for time
BS is the crude abbreviation for nonsense

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that some modern art wins admirers only for its crude nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The first T of ATTRACTS is replaced by BS, giving ABSTRACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstracts are non-representational paintings or sculptures, a staple of modern art galleries.

clue.text: Soft leather is taken from chamois, tanned

indicators.note: the little word is is lifted out of the longer word it sits in
to tan can mean to beat, and a beaten word has its letters knocked about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A leather worker notes that soft leather comes from chamois skins after tanning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanned' reads as the leather process, but here it means beaten, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine soft suede-like leather made from sheepskin or goatskin.

clue.text: Youthful courtier robing king, one showing high birth

indicators.note: robing someone wraps a garment round them, so one word is put around the others

blocks.note: a page is a boy attendant at court
R for rex, king
a means one

explanation.surface: A young courtier dresses the king, a sign of the attendant's noble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGE goes around R and A to give PARAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Parage is an old word for lineage, especially noble descent or rank by birth.

clue.text: Passerines: I caught eastern one in course of journey

indicators.note: something in the course of a thing sits within it, so one letter goes inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
CT is a cricket abbreviation for caught
E for eastern
a ride is a journey
a means one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports catching an eastern songbird partway through a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the birdwatcher's verb, but it is the cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Icteridae is the family of New World perching birds such as orioles and blackbirds, all passerines.

clue.text: Australian fills tub in shallow lake locally?

indicators.note: whatever fills a vessel ends up inside it

blocks.note: a cowl is an old word for a large tub or water vessel
A for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian climbs into a tub at a shallow lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' with its question mark points to an Australian regional word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage a cowal is a shallow lake or swampy depression.

clue.text: Food prepared in task, private (11, two words)

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: tommy is an old word for food or bread, especially soldiers' rations
the letters of in task rearranged

explanation.surface: Food being cooked in a task set for a private soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a soldier of lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Atkins is the traditional nickname for a typical British private soldier.

clue.text: One supporting band on tour in Spain after radio broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seed is, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of radio rearranged
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A tour crew member in Spain helps the band after a radio session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places E at the end of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie is a member of a touring band's crew who carries and sets up the equipment.

clue.text: Inexperienced female, natural, in being moved to take the lead

indicators.text: being moved to take the lead
indicators.note: being moved shifts the two letters from their place and sets them at the front of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
natural and genuine both mean real, unaffected

explanation.surface: A natural young actress is promoted to the leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is lifted out of GENUINE and put at the front, giving INGENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, artless young woman, especially that stock role on stage.

clue.text: Keep exotic fish in private room

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a den is a private retreat or study
the tai is a Japanese sea bream

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an exotic fish in a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to hold or keep them back.

clue.text: Once calm, listener may have heard this from a troubadour

linkWords: listener may have heard this from

blocks.note: taken as written
a lay is a song or ballad, what a troubadour sings

explanation.surface: A listener soothed by a troubadour's song.
explanation.walkthrough: The listener hears 'a lay', a song, from the wandering minstrel; 'once' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alay is an old spelling of allay, to soothe or quieten.

clue.text: Tree, Australian, planted in dip

indicators.note: something planted in soil goes inside it

blocks.note: to bob is to dip quickly, as in a curtsey
A for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian tree is planted in a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: The boab is the Australian baobab, a tree with a hugely swollen trunk.

clue.text: Features of club tea? There's a bit of a fiddle with name lists (11, two words)

blocks.note: the bridge is the part of a violin that holds the strings up
rolls are registers of names

explanation.surface: A club tea where someone fiddles the membership lists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the club may be a bridge club serving its own namesake buns.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge rolls are small soft finger-shaped bread rolls typical of buffet or club teas.

clue.text: Without others, as of old, where Hereward took refuge?

blocks.note: on gives the location, as in on an island
Hereward the Wake held out against William the Conqueror on the Isle of Ely, in the Fens of eastern England

explanation.surface: A history question: where did the outlaw Hereward hide alone?
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'on Ely', where Hereward took refuge; 'as of old' marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Onely is an obsolete spelling of only, meaning alone, with nobody else.

clue.text: Singular crop – millions graze locally

blocks.note: S for singular
the craw is a bird's crop
M for millions

explanation.surface: A farmer notes an unusual crop while millions of animals graze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' suggests a harvest, but it is the pouch in a bird's throat; 'graze' means scratch, not feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawm is a dialect word meaning to scratch or scrape the skin.

clue.text: Newspaper's label for the common herd

blocks.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A tabloid's dismissive name for ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, means the rabble, the lowest common people.

clue.text: In the morning loads Indian set meal receptacles

indicators.note: a thing that loads another takes it on board, holding it inside

blocks.note: a thali is an Indian meal of several small dishes on one tray
AM means in the morning

explanation.surface: A breakfast thali is served loaded onto platters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receptacles' sounds like dishes, but it is the botanical sense: the part of a flower stalk bearing the floral organs.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a thalamus is the receptacle of a flower, so thalami are receptacles.

clue.text: Bit of cloth held by Titian shaping ear parts

indicators.note: a thing held by another is gripped inside it
shaping moulds material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the painter's name rearranged
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: The painter Titian holds a cloth while modelling the ears of a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: An antitragus is the small fleshy knob of the outer ear opposite the tragus; antitragi is the plural.

clue.text: With stubby projections on shield, silver, held by orderly

indicators.note: a thing held by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: ruly, the rare opposite of unruly, means orderly
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A knight's shield, silver and studded, carried by a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like the hospital worker but is the adjective, neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Raguly is a heraldic term for a line or charge with short stubs like a lopped branch.

clue.text: Lump on the head, or wing? Not positive at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is lost, and that letter is the abbreviation for positive

blocks.note: a pinion is a bird's wing
P for positive, then dropped

explanation.surface: A doctor wonders whether a bump on the head is really a stray wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The inion is the bony knob at the back of the skull, the external occipital protuberance.

clue.text: Part of US trunk-call charge, minutes and ages being treated differently (11, two words)

indicators.note: treated differently means handled in a new way, so these letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A long-distance call bill charges for minutes, while ages on hold are billed some other way.
explanation.walkthrough: A trunk call is the British term for a long-distance phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a message unit was a measure of telephone usage on which toll charges were based.

clue.text: Tons left in net, what fishermen suspend from buoys

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: T for tons
L for left
a seine is a large fishing net

explanation.surface: Tons of catch left in the net, by gear hung from buoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A setline is a long fishing line carrying many hooks, anchored and held by buoys.

clue.text: ENT meet for treatment, in short – it involves internal scouring

indicators.note: letters up for treatment are worked on and come out in a new order
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: curt means short, brusque
the letters of ENT meet rearranged

explanation.surface: Ear, nose and throat specialists meet briefly to discuss a scraping procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department; 'in short' reads as 'briefly' but says 'inside a word for short'.
explanation.definitionFit: Curettement is the surgical scraping of a body cavity with a curette.

clue.text: After run out, shot to leg lifted MCG attendance?

indicators.note: in a down clue a lifted word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

blocks.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
a pull is a cricket shot hit to the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a run-out and a shot to leg before the crowd at the Melbourne ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The MCG is the Melbourne Cricket Ground; 'after' puts the turned-round shot after RO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a roll-up is the number of people who turn up, the attendance.

clue.text: A spot of laryngitis which holds tenor up, number abandoned

indicators.note: a thing that holds another has it inside
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top
a number word is dropped from the voice part that precedes it

blocks.note: that and which are both relative pronouns
taken as written
ten is a number, then dropped

explanation.surface: A singer's laryngitis has the tenor dropping out of the number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like the song the tenor sings, but it is the number word cut from the front of tenor. 'A spot' means a place where laryngitis strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx, located in the throat.

clue.text: Medicinal application I smear after start of nettle-rash

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: first letter of nettle-rash
taken as written
to moil is an old word for to daub or bedaub

explanation.surface: I rub on a soothing ointment after the first itch of a nettle rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Nim oil, from the neem tree, is used medicinally on the skin.

clue.text: Faith displayed by husband? Wrong, in hindsight

indicators.note: hindsight is looking back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: H for husband
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A husband's fidelity proves, looking back, to have been misplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is an old word for faith or loyalty, as in plighting one's troth.

clue.text: Buck spends life in lodge

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to lodge is to settle, stay or rest
to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A male deer lives out its days in a hunting lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like the male deer but is the verb: to buck a trend is to oppose it.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck something is to fight against it or oppose it.

clue.text: Leader of upper house has left, developing external constituents?

indicators.note: a letter that has left is gone from the word

blocks.note: the senate is the upper house of many parliaments
the leading letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: The upper house's leader has resigned, and outside members are building a power base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' here means components, not voters; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Enate is a botanical term for growing outwards, as of outgrowths from a surface.

clue.text: Money maybe raised to instigate drainage flow

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase of purpose, describing a thing used to start drainage

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: banknotes are one form of money

explanation.surface: Cash is raised to start a drainage project.
explanation.definitionFit: A seton is a thread passed through the skin to keep a wound or fistula draining.

clue.text: Get soused around afternoon in bar, often

indicators.note: one thing set around another surrounds it

blocks.note: to sop is to soak or drench
A is short for afternoon, as in p.m.

explanation.surface: Getting drunk all afternoon in a pub, as a regular habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a bar of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap is commonly sold and used as a solid bar.

clue.text: In Romeo you'll see misguided result of long-term bonding

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: the letters of in Romeo rearranged

explanation.surface: Romeo's misguided passion ends in a lasting union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-term bonding' reads as romance but means chemical bonds along long polymer chains.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionomer is a polymer whose long chains are linked by ionic bonds.

clue.text: Unaccompanied performances close to amplifier

blocks.note: soli is a plural of solo
on means next to, close to

explanation.surface: Solo performers playing right up beside the amp.
explanation.definitionFit: A solion is an electrochemical device that detects and amplifies small electrical currents.

clue.text: Native American language without issue? Reverse of that

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

blocks.note: atokal is a zoological term for having no young

explanation.surface: A tribal language with no descendants, read the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lakota is the language of the Lakota Sioux people of the northern Great Plains.

clue.text: Bum holding one back? One gets all steamed up

indicators.note: a thing holding another has it inside
going back means the result is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: bum here is the backside
a means one

explanation.surface: A layabout keeps someone waiting, and that person gets furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All steamed up' sounds like anger but literally describes a steam room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a hot steam bath room, so it is a place full of steam.

clue.text: I tucked into traditional stodge – it's often potted

indicators.note: a thing tucked into another is pushed inside it

blocks.note: bog is an older sense of stodge, a thick sticky mire
taken as written

explanation.surface: I dug into a traditional stodgy pudding, the sort often served in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potted' suggests food, but a potted biography is a brief summary of a life.
explanation.definitionFit: A biog is a short biography, and short life histories are often called potted biographies.

clue.text: Antipasto? Favourite is wrapped in e.g. onion-skin (no starter)

indicators.note: with no starter the word loses its opening letter
something wrapped in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: onion-skin is a thin translucent paper
a pet is a favourite
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's favourite starter comes wrapped in onion skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Onion-skin is a thin translucent writing paper, not the vegetable's peel; the starter that goes is the first letter of that paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course, a classic appetiser before the main meal.
